a
This is Murshid. It helps students get their work done and stay on top of it: every class, assignment, test and activity, in one plan.
b
There are two ways to get Murshid. A parent can buy it for their child, or a student for themselves. But our main focus is schools: a school licenses Murshid for every one of its students.
c
In the proposed Grade 11 pilot at Our Own High School Al Warqa'a, the school would connect Microsoft 365 once, Teams classes come in, and teachers sign in with Microsoft (simulated in this demo).
d
Mr. Desai posts an assignment to his maths class. It goes to all thirty students at once. On Ahamed's side, it's already in today's plan, and on his School page, marked new.
e
Murshid reads each student's work across all their subjects, plus tests, sport and events, and gives the teacher a class report: who's on track, who's at risk, and why.
f
It suggests how to hand out the next task: support for four students, more time for Ahamed, whose week is full of fixtures, and extension work for nine.
g
And it finds the best day to set homework. Set it Tuesday, due Thursday: eighty-seven percent likely on time, clear of the economics mid-term and Friday's athletics heats.
h
Every Friday, each student's weekly report sends itself, and rolls up here for the teacher.
i

For students, Murshid plans the week around tests and training, showing each step in plain words as it checks their timetable. And it finds opportunities that fit, like a young founders pitch night for Ahamed's business.
j
Murshid for Schools. Every student on top of their work, and every teacher with the full picture.
